sentence: This project studies how phthalates cause females to go through reproductive aging early.
This project tests whether dogs differ from humans in DNA damage, damage repair and cell death, to explain their higher rate of somatic mutation.
This project develops a gene editing therapy for the vision loss that comes with Usher Syndrome, testing it in a rabbit model.
This project studies how poor blood supply to transplanted lungs could cause inflammation and destroy airway cells, leading to scarring in small airways.
This project provides a shared resource for imaging animals and humans.
This project examines whether phthalates and bisphenols change reproductive hormone levels and anogenital distance in infants during minipuberty.
This project provides bioinformatic and biostatistical support for analyzing multi-omics data from animal models and patients.
This project develops small molecules that block binding to RNA, to test whether this can slow or reverse harmful tau buildup.
This project develops a way to take prostate diffusion-weighted images that are sharp and free of distortion using rapid acquisition and advanced reconstruction.
This project measures how genetic differences between cells build up with age, using whole genome sequencing of human colon crypt samples.
This project studies how DNA regions inherited from the mother and father interact to control gene expression in stem cells.
This project tries to find out what a gene does and how losing it kills rhabdoid cells, a type of childhood tumor.
This project builds a robotic endoscope holder that uses computer vision to make surgical navigation more precise and to update patient anatomy as surgery proceeds.
This project studies how a signaling protein controls survival of pancreatic cancer cells and shapes the fibroblasts and immune cells around them.
This project tries to find out which proteins control how cells lining blood vessels release von Willebrand factor.
This project tries to find out whether early changes in hippocampal network activity in CLN3 disease limit gene therapy, and whether changing network activity helps.
This project studies how low oxygen in cells lining kidney blood vessels changes their metabolism and affects kidney repair after acute kidney injury.
This project builds RNA-targeting CRISPR tools that can write changes into RNA without off-target collateral activity in cells.
This project develops a gene therapy for hemophilia A that makes factor VIII in blood platelets to give therapeutic protein and immune tolerance.
